title: The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US?
summary:
The Falklands dispute: What’s it got to do with Israel and the US?

Argentina has restated its claim to sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a small rocky archipelago in the South Atlantic that is owned by the UK.  

Javier Milei, the far-right president of Argentina, said in a national address on Thursday that the "winds of change" favoured his country’s claim to the islands, and threatened sanctions on oil firms that seek to drill in the territory’s waters. "We need to recover these islands which are nationally relevant," he said. 

The announcement comes days after US President Donald Trump suggested that he is reviewing the US position on UK sovereignty, known in Argentina as Las Islas Malvinas.

“I always review every position - that’s just one of many,” Trump told reporters in the White House. “The UK’s got some problems, but they’ll get solved."

The future of the sparsely inhabited islands has been speculated on for months amid tensions between Washington and London about UK military commitments, including the war on Iran.

title: Turkish spy chief makes secretive visit to Greece amid rising tensions with Israel, report says
summary:
Turkish spy chief makes secretive visit to Greece amid rising tensions with Israel, report says

Submitted by MEE staff on Sun, 09/06/2026 - 12:39
The development comes amid strained relations over the Aegean Sea as Greece deepens its defence partnership with Israel
Turkish presidential adviser Ibrahim Kalin speaks to AFP journalists during an interview in Istanbul, 13 November 2021. (Ozan Kose/AFP)
Off

Turkey’s intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin made a secret visit to Athens last week for talks with his Greek counterpart, Greek and Turkish media have reported.

According to a report by Greek newspaper Ta Nea, Kalin, head of Turkey’s National Intelligence Organisation (MIT), met Themistoklis Demiris, director of Greece’s National Intelligence Service (EYP).

The development comes amid renewed tensions over the Aegean Sea, deepening Greece-Israel defence ties and wider security concerns in the Eastern Mediterranean. 

Greece and Turkey have been in dispute over maritime borders, the status and militarisation of Aegean islands and Cyprus. 

The latest intelligence-level contact comes days after Greece and Israel signed a $3.5bn defence deal under which Israel will help Athens develop a multi-layered air defence system known as Achilles Shield. 

It includes Israel’s David’s Sling and SPYDER systems, the Barak MX air-defence system and MMR multi-mission radars.

The broader Greek air defence programme is worth $28bn and is expected to be finished by 2036.

The growing Greece-Israel defence relationship has become a source of concern in Ankara as tensions between Turkey and Israel have increased over developments in the region.

Ankara protests Athens' deployment of US-made armoured vehicles on two islands
Read More »

The visit was not made public, and details of the reported visit were published by Turkish news website Yeni Şafak.

In his analysis in Yeni Şafak on Saturday, columnist Yahya Bostan said Kalin relayed Ankara’s position that Turkey wanted to preserve a constructive relationship with Greece, while also insisting on its rights and interests.

Turkey will not accept unilateral steps that create a fait accompli in the Aegean or change what Ankara views as the current status quo through the militarisation of islands, according to Bostan.

Ankara, according to the report, saw attempts by Greece to establish a new security line in the region via Israel as “the wrong way”.

The report said Turkey also warned it wasn’t a threat to Greece but would not accept developments undermining its rights and interests. 

Greek accounts told a rather different story of the visit, emphasising intelligence and security cooperation.

According to Greek City Times, the talks focused on organised crime, migrant-smuggling networks, terrorism and espionage.

The talks reportedly involved the presence in Greece of some 300 Turkish organised crime figures, linked to some 15 criminal organisations, as well as Turkish nationals allegedly involved in organising migrant-smuggling operations from the Turkish coast. 

Turkey-Greece tensions: A clash of nationalisms
Read More »

The meeting was reportedly held through a regular security link between Athens and Ankara.

Ankara has also objected to Greek initiatives in the Aegean, including its Special Spatial Framework for Tourism.

In August, Turkey’s foreign ministry said the Greek framework had no legal consequences for Ankara and urged Athens not to take unilateral actions in the Aegean and Mediterranean. 

“We once again emphasise that attempts to instrumentalise universal values such as environmental protection for political purposes are futile and will in no way affect our country's established legal position,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Oncu Keceli told Anadolu Agency.

Keceli also said that international maritime law encourages cooperation between coastal states in enclosed and semi-enclosed seas, including on environmental issues.

Kalin has been the head of MIT since June 2023, when his predecessor Hakan Fidan became Turkey’s foreign minister.

For years, Kalin was a senior adviser and close foreign policy aide to President Recep Tayyip Erdogan before becoming the head of the intelligence agency.

Greece and Turkey have kept open lines of communication between their intelligence and police services despite decades of political and strategic disagreements.

In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses."

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. title: Using a VM to Contain an AI Agent
summary:
It won’t work:

My suspicion was that GPT 5.6-Cyber would succeed, but the frequency and manner of its success removed all doubt. We have to reassess sandboxing quality for capable AI agents, and in general the software stack with which they interact.

An off-the-shelf VM is not enough to contain a modern, cyber-capable AI agent. There is simply too much attack surface. Even innocuous features (like running with a display) add extra, exploitable attack surface.

title: Security Vulnerability in a Voting System
summary:
It’s a vulnerability that allows someone to recover the order of ballots cast, newly exploited with AI tools.

Nearly four years since the original vulnerability was disclosed, I was still able to use it to analyze voter behavior in Georgia (one of the 21 states that uses affected scanners) in the recent May 2026 primary.

Notably, I never touched a voting machine, exploited a network, examined source code, or accessed anything non-public.

After pointing a coding agent to the original vulnerability paper, I supplied it with two data sources highlighted in the paper: the early-voting list for each county, and the “CVR” (cast-vote record) file, containing every ballot and its selections (but not the voters’ names or other identifying information). The CVR file is available upon request, precisely because a public, ballot-level record is what makes election results independently verifiable...

title: AI Coding Agents Are Installing Unknown/Untrusted Code on Corporate Networks
summary:
We cannot forget that AI coding agents are not yet trustworthy:

Researchers at a stealth startup in Israel scanned 6,214 live domains belonging to defense contractors, Fortune 500, and Big Tech companies. Of the 8,265 llms.txt and llms-full.txt files they found (many sites hosted both an llms.txt and an llms-full.txt file), 120 of them, each on a different site, pointed to one or more code packages or domain names that weren’t registered. To test what happens when an AI agent processes such files, the researchers registered a handful of the unclaimed names and hosted packages that caused any machine executing them to reach out to their server. Within an hour, the researchers received a phone-home response from a Fortune 500 company. Over time, they got a few dozen more, some from more Fortune 500 companies and others from startups. Their beacon also recorded the chain of parent processes that spawned each install, ultimately revealing that coding agents, including Claude, OpenAI’s Codex, and Nous Research’s Hermes, were involved. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nous Research did not respond to requests for comment by the time of publication...

title: Gaza death toll rises to 73,651 since October 2023
summary:
Gaza death toll rises to 73,651 since October 2023

The death toll from Israel's genocide in Gaza has risen to 73,651, while the number of wounded has reached 174,592 since 7 October 2023, according to Palestinian health authorities.

Hospitals across Gaza reported that the number of Palestinians killed since the ceasefire took effect on 11 October has risen to 1,344, while 4,481 others have been wounded.

A total of 826 bodies have also been recovered, while thousands of Palestinians remain buried under the rubble.

title: Iran threatens South Korean assets if Seoul joins Hormuz mission
summary:
Iran threatens South Korean assets if Seoul joins Hormuz mission

Iranian academic Mohammad Marandi has warned that Tehran would consider South Korea an enemy and could strike its economic and military interests across the Persian Gulf if Seoul joins the US-led war on Iran.

Speaking on Al Mayadeen’s The Grand Standoff, Marandi said South Korea’s involvement in efforts to secure freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz would expose its interests in the region to Iranian retaliation.

“If the South Koreans participate in this war against Iran, Iran will see it as the enemy,” Marandi said, adding that Tehran would seek to “destroy whatever assets South Korea has in this region”.

Those targets would not necessarily be military installations, he said, and Iranian strikes could include South Korean assets in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar.

“So the Koreans are very vulnerable to Iran,” said Marandi. “Iran can hurt them very badly.”

Read more: Iran threatens South Korean assets if Seoul joins Hormuz mission

title: Eight foreign ministers condemn Katz and Ben Gvir’s Gaza displacement plan
summary:
Eight foreign ministers condemn Katz and Ben Gvir’s Gaza displacement plan

The foreign ministers of eight countries have condemned statements and plans by Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir for the mass expulsion of Palestinians from Gaza.

In a joint statement, the foreign ministers of the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkey and Egypt said the proposals are a flagrant violation of international law and pose a direct threat to the inalienable rights of Palestinians.

The Israeli ministers floated proposals this week for the removal of Palestinians from the besieged enclave, with Ben Gvir laying out a seven-year plan for displacement through "voluntary emigration". 

He said he would seek the creation of a "ministry in charge of emigration" in the next government.

The foreign ministers urged the international community, particularly the UN Security Council, to oppose any attempts to impose a new demographic or territorial reality in Gaza.

title: Iran's response to US attacks will be 'faster, more painful', Ghalibaf says
summary:
Iran's response to US attacks will be 'faster, more painful', Ghalibaf says

The US should understand that the rules of the game in the war with Iran have changed "before it is too late", Iranian parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has said.

"From now on, any attack against Iran’s interests and security will receive a faster, heavier and more painful response,” he said, in a speech published on his Telegram channel.
